Ben / Marissa — forwarding Maya's note and usage. My read: they need runway to complete validation and they want to avoid throttling while procurement issues a PO. Procurement is already looped.

Suggested options to present (I prefer 1 or 2):
1) Short extension + one-time token credit: 3-week extension to Dec 26 + 25M token credit applied immediately. No change to per-token price; credits cover immediate overage.
   - Internal cost: one-time credit (we should quantify in dollars if needed).
   - Rationale: keeps them working without changing long-term pricing.
2) 4-week extension + 15% discount on any overage tokens during the extension window if they commit to a Jan conversion (convert = committed monthly minimum).
3) Temporary small reserved pool (Dedicated-style) for the duration of the pilot at a discounted short-term rate — higher ops overhead, slower to provision.

Which option are you comfortable approving today? If we go with 1, I can draft an amendment and send to Maya + procurement. I'll attach a simple offer summary for numbers.

Hi Maya — thanks for the details. Based on your numbers and procurement timeline, here are two pragmatic options we can implement within 24–48 hours:

Option A (recommended): 3-week extension (new end date: 2026-12-26) + one-time 25,000,000 token credit applied immediately.
- How this works: we add an amendment that extends the pilot term by 21 days and posts 25M tokens to your account. Any additional consumption beyond credits during the extension will be billed at your current pilot overage rate.
- Conversion incentive: if Lumina converts to an annual committed arrangement by Jan 31, we will rebate 50% of the credit value as a one-time invoice credit on first bill.

Option B: 4-week extension (ends 2027-01-02) + 15% discount on overage tokens during the extension.

Practical notes:
- We can issue a short amendment (attached draft) and route via DocuSign for signature.
- If procurement prefers a PO instead of DocuSign, we can accept a PO and provision credits once PO is received, but that means a short gap risk.

Next step: confirm which option you prefer and procurement contact for PO processing. I've attached a draft amendment for Option A to speed approvers.

Thanks,
Hannah
